entries.name: GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID
entries.description: OAuth client for Gmail and Google Drive access.
howToGet: In console.cloud.google.com, create a project, enable the Gmail and Drive APIs, and create an OAuth client ID (Web application).

entries.name: GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET
entries.description: Secret for the Google OAuth client.
howToGet: Shown next to the OAuth client ID in Google Cloud Console > APIs & Services > Credentials.

entries.name: GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI
entries.description: Where Google sends the owner back after granting access.
howToGet: Use https://<instance-host>/oauth/google/callback and add it to the OAuth client's authorized redirect URIs.

entries.name: CUSTOMER_REF_KEY
entries.description: Key for customer references: a keyed hash (HMAC-SHA256) of a customer's id in a system, email address or phone number, so one customer's records link up across systems without the id or any contact detail being stored. Changing it breaks those links, so it is never rotated.
howToGet: Generated automatically by npm run secrets:setup. Keep a copy in the password manager: losing it means a customer's earlier records no longer link to new ones.

entries.name: CORRESPONDENT_HASH_KEY
entries.description: The instance's own key for turning people's identifiers (email addresses, Slack user ids) into private references (HMAC-SHA256), so the brain can tell that two messages or appointments involve the same person without keeping who they are. Without the key, a reference can't be matched against a guessed identifier.
howToGet: Generated automatically by npm run secrets:setup.
Don't rotate it unless a leak is suspected: a new key gives every person a new reference, so earlier history no longer lines up with later messages and appointments.
